steps.description: Sort arrivals [900, 940, 950, 1100, 1500, 1800] and departures [910, 1120, 1130, 1200, 1900, 2000] independently, then read them as ONE timeline: every A is a train arriving, every D is one leaving. Which train each event belongs to stops mattering from here - only the order does.

The first event on the timeline is always an arrival, so start with 1 platform in use. A marks the next arrival, D the earliest departure not yet passed - those two cells are the only ones ever compared.
Which comes first on the timeline: the next arrival at 940, or the earliest still-open departure at 910?
The departure wins: 940 > 910, so a train leaves before the next one arrives. A platform frees up: 0 in use. Step D forward.
Highest platform count seen so far: 1.
Which comes first on the timeline: the next arrival at 940, or the earliest still-open departure at 1120?
The arrival wins: 940 <= 1120, so that train pulls in before any platform frees up. One more platform is needed: 1. Step A forward.
Highest platform count seen so far: 1.
Which comes first on the timeline: the next arrival at 950, or the earliest still-open departure at 1120?
The arrival wins: 950 <= 1120, so that train pulls in before any platform frees up. One more platform is needed: 2. Step A forward.
Highest platform count seen so far: 2.

The arrival wins: 1100 <= 1120, so that train pulls in before any platform frees up. One more platform is needed: 3. Step A forward.
Highest platform count seen so far: 3.
